title: When you are grieving
line: For loss of any kind: a person, a relationship, a life you expected.
intro: Grief is love with nowhere to go. This practice does not try to make it smaller. It gives it a few quiet minutes, a lamp, and words that have held grieving people for thousands of years.

steps.title: Arrive
steps.text: Breathe slowly, and let the out-breath be a little longer than the in-breath. There is no right way to feel.

steps.title: Light the lamp
steps.text: Light a lamp for the one you have lost, or for what you have lost.

steps.title: Words for the deepest self
steps.text: Krishna’s words on the self that is not born and does not die. Read them slowly. They are a perspective to hold, never an instruction to stop grieving.

steps.title: Something to hold on to
steps.text: Repeat AUM Namah Shivaya softly, or simply breathe with it.

steps.title: Remember
steps.text: You may write it here, kept only on this device, or simply hold it.
steps.prompt: A memory I want to keep, or something I wish I could say.

steps.title: Close
steps.text: Read the closing prayer once, slowly. Then sit for one more breath before you return to your day.

after: Grief comes in waves; come back whenever you need. If it feels too heavy to carry, please talk to someone: in India, Tele-MANAS is free on 14416, day and night.
